_how_to_edit: Every CASA audit item must appear exactly once. status = verified | not_applicable | pending. verified needs evidence (test:<fn>, lint:<rule>, tool:<name>, file:<path>) or an attestation {by,date,artifact}. not_applicable needs reason + reopen_if regexes that fail the gate if matching code appears. pending needs a blocker and fails release builds (CASA_STRICT=1). After editing run: python3 scripts/casa_check.py render

requirements.title: Authentication is resistant to brute force attacks
requirements.blocker: No authentication yet (Google OAuth sign-in not built). Per-client rate limiting already protects every endpoint; re-verify on the OAuth callback once it exists.

requirements.title: System generated initial passwords or activation codes are securely random and expire quickly
requirements.reason: The app issues no passwords or activation codes; sign-in is delegated to Google.

requirements.title: Passwords are stored in a form resistant to offline attacks
requirements.reason: The app never receives or stores user passwords; sign-in is delegated to Google.

requirements.title: Default credentials are not present on publicly exposed interfaces
requirements.notes: Migrations seed no accounts. .env.example ships an empty POSTGRES_PASSWORD, and docker-compose refuses to start until it is set. Postgres binds to 127.0.0.1 only.

requirements.title: Out of band verifier expires in a reasonable timeframe
requirements.reason: No SMS, email or other out-of-band verification codes are issued.

requirements.title: Out of band verifier is only used once
requirements.reason: No out-of-band verifiers are issued.

requirements.title: Out of band verifier is securely random
requirements.reason: No out-of-band verifiers are issued.

requirements.title: Out of band verifier is resistant to brute force attacks
requirements.reason: No out-of-band verifiers are issued.

requirements.title: Passwords, session tokens and API keys are not exposed in URL parameters
Users can log out; logout or expiry invalidates all stateful session tokens, including refresh tokens
requirements.blocker: Sessions do not exist yet. Build them with the OAuth login: server-side session table, a logout endpoint that deletes the row, and idle/absolute expiry.

requirements.title: Other sessions can be terminated after a password change or reset
requirements.reason: The app has no passwords; credential changes happen at Google. Revisit if local accounts are added.

requirements.title: Non-revocable stateless authentication tokens expire within 24 hours
requirements.blocker: Session design pending. Prefer opaque, revocable server-side sessions; any JWT must have exp <= 24h.

requirements.title: Cookie-based session tokens have the Secure attribute
requirements.blocker: No session cookie yet. lint:cookie-flags already rejects any cookie built without secure(true), http_only(true) and same_site.

requirements.title: Cookie-based session tokens have the HttpOnly attribute
requirements.blocker: No session cookie yet. lint:cookie-flags already enforces http_only(true).

requirements.title: Session tokens are used rather than static API secrets and keys
requirements.blocker: Authentication not built. Use per-user session tokens; do not add static shared API keys for clients.

requirements.title: Stateless session tokens are protected against tampering, replay, null cipher and key substitution
requirements.blocker: Session design pending. If stateless tokens are chosen, pin the algorithm, reject alg=none and validate iss/aud/exp.

requirements.title: A full valid session or re-authentication is required before sensitive transactions or account changes
requirements.blocker: Authentication not built. All state-changing endpoints must require a valid session.

requirements.title: Least-privilege access control rules are enforced on a trusted service layer
requirements.blocker: BLOCKER: /api/notes is unauthenticated. Any client can list, read and delete every note. Add OAuth sessions, a notes.owner_id column, and scope every query to the session user.

requirements.title: User and data attributes used by access controls cannot be manipulated by end users
requirements.notes: Every request body struct uses deny_unknown_fields, so server-controlled fields such as id, created_at and (later) owner_id cannot be mass-assigned.

requirements.title: Access controls fail securely, including when an exception occurs
requirements.blocker: No access control layer yet. Existing controls fail closed (missing limiter returns 500; internal errors are masked). Extend this to the auth middleware.

requirements.title: Sensitive resources are protected against IDOR on create, read, update and delete
requirements.blocker: BLOCKER: GET/DELETE /api/notes/{id} perform no ownership check. Fix together with 3.1.1.

requirements.title: Strong anti-CSRF protects authenticated functionality; anti-automation or anti-CSRF protects unauthenticated functionality
requirements.notes: State-changing endpoints accept only application/json, which a cross-site form cannot send without a CORS preflight, and no CORS is granted. Re-check when session cookies are added (SameSite is enforced by lint:cookie-flags).

requirements.title: Directory browsing is disabled
Only secure OAuth 2.0 flows (Authorization Code, with PKCE) are used; implicit and password grants are not
requirements.blocker: Google OAuth not built yet. lint:oauth-implicit-flow already rejects response_type=token and grant_type=password.

requirements.title: redirect_uri and state are validated during OAuth authorization
requirements.blocker: Google OAuth not built yet. Use a fixed, registered redirect_uri; generate a random state, bind it to the pre-auth session and compare it on callback.

requirements.title: Application administrative interfaces use multi-factor authentication
requirements.reason: The application exposes no administrative interface.

requirements.title: TLS is enforced for all connections (TLS 1.2+, secure cipher suites)
requirements.blocker: nginx listens on plain HTTP :80. Terminate TLS 1.2+ at nginx or the load balancer, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, enable HSTS in nginx/security-headers.conf, then record an SSL Labs report as an attestation.

requirements.title: Connections to and from the server use trusted TLS certificates
requirements.blocker: Depends on 4.1.1. The backend-to-Postgres link is plaintext on the private compose network; use sslmode=verify-full for any managed or remote database.

requirements.title: No weak cryptography affecting confidential data
Cryptographic modules fail securely; no padding oracles
requirements.reason: The application performs no encryption or decryption of its own (TLS is handled by rustls and nginx).

requirements.title: Protect against HTTP parameter pollution
URL redirects and forwards are limited to allowlisted URLs
requirements.notes: The application performs no redirects. The OAuth login will add one; it must target a constant URL and carry a suppression with a justification.

requirements.title: No eval() or other dynamic code execution
Protect against template injection
requirements.reason: No server-side templating. The UI is compiled SolidJS JSX, which escapes text by default.

requirements.title: Prevent server-side request forgery
requirements.reason: The backend makes no outbound HTTP requests.

requirements.title: Protect against XPath or XML injection
requirements.reason: No XML is parsed or produced.

requirements.title: Context-aware output escaping protects against reflected, stored and DOM XSS
requirements.notes: API: JSON only, nosniff, CSP default-src 'none', set by the backend alone (nginx adds no headers to proxied /api/ responses). UI: Solid escapes interpolations, raw HTML sinks are banned, strict CSP from nginx.

requirements.title: Protect against database injection
requirements.notes: All SQL is static text with sqlx bind parameters.

requirements.title: Protect against OS command injection
Protect against local and remote file inclusion
Uploads are limited to expected types and never executed
requirements.reason: No file upload functionality.

requirements.title: Only components without known exploitable vulnerabilities are used
Debug modes are disabled in production
The Origin header is not used for authentication or access control decisions
The application is not susceptible to subdomain takeover
requirements.blocker: Deployment and DNS are not defined yet. Before assessment, audit DNS for dangling CNAMEs and record it as an attestation.

requirements.title: Credentials and payment details are not logged; session tokens appear in logs only hashed
Browser storage is securely cleared during logout
requirements.notes: Nothing is written to localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB or document.cookie from JS, and the lint keeps it that way.

requirements.title: Access tokens, API keys and other server-side secrets are stored securely
requirements.blocker: In code, secrets come only from the environment, .env is git-ignored, and gitleaks runs on every commit. Production still needs a secrets manager (encrypted, access-controlled, audited); record it as an attestation.

requirements.title: Webhook communications use HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ only
requirements.reason: The application neither sends nor receives webhooks.

requirements.title: Webhook providers verify endpoint ownership before delivering events
requirements.reason: The application neither sends nor receives webhooks.

requirements.title: Webhook payloads are authenticated with HMAC-SHA256 or stronger
requirements.reason: The application neither sends nor receives webhooks.

requirements.title: Webhook signature verification uses timing-safe comparison
requirements.reason: The application neither sends nor receives webhooks.

requirements.title: Webhook payloads include replay protection via signed timestamps
requirements.reason: The application neither sends nor receives webhooks.

requirements.title: Webhook providers mitigate SSRF for user-supplied callback URLs
requirements.reason: The application neither sends nor receives webhooks.

requirements.title: Webhook signing secrets are not hardcoded or stored in version control
requirements.reason: The application neither sends nor receives webhooks.
